title: 5 Fresh Digital Marketing Ideas for Financial Advisors in 2026
summary: What worked a few years ago represents just the minimum of what an advisor's digital marketing strategy should be doing in 2026.
body_markdown:
Digital marketing has become an essential growth tool for financial advisors, but success depends on choosing the right strategies. What worked just a few years ago, including traditional SEO, email marketing and social media, represents the baseline for what an advisor should be doing to make their brand more noticeable in a competitive marketplace. The next wave of digital marketing tactics focuses largely on five factors: artificial intelligence, thought leadership, local search visibility, short-form content and compliance-aware social posting.

## 1. Let AI Do the Heavy Lifting


AI continues to make inroads in the financial services space, and investors are taking notice. A majority, 71%, of advised clients say they expect their advisor to use[AI tools](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/ai-tools-for-financial-advisors) for at least one purpose, according to 2025 Million Dollar Roundtable study.1 Some of the most common use cases for AI in a digital marketing plan include:


**Content Creation** Generative AI can brainstorm and draft blog posts, social content and other marketing materials, or repurpose existing content into new formats.


**Workflow Automation** AI tools can help manage content calendars, email campaigns and[social media scheduling](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/social-media-calendar-for-financial-advisors) , while CRM integrations can track and store workflow data.


**Client Service and Meeting Support** AI can summarize meeting notes, draft follow-up emails and help organize client information, giving advisors more time to focus on client relationships.


Note that any AI-generated content is subject to the same strict compliance review as content you create yourself. Content should be verified for accuracy, per the[SEC’s marketing rule](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/sec-marketing-rule-faqs) .

## 2. Position Yourself as an Expert


Ninety-six percent of investors do their own research when choosing an advisor, versus relying on referrals alone, according to a 2025 Wealthtender survey of households making $100,000+ annually.2 They look for advisors with a solid digital footprint and reputation, the survey found.


Cultivating a public image as a[thought leader](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-services-thought-leadership) can support other arms of your digital marketing plan, including social media and your website. Thought leaders are recognized experts on a particular topic. For example,[Michael Kitces](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-influencers) is considered to be a thought leader in the financial advisor marketing and business development space.


Some of the ways advisors can position themselves as thought leaders include:


- Selecting a single topic or related group of topics to focus on
- Conducting original research around that topic and sharing results on[LinkedIn](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/linkedin-marketing-for-financial-advisors) and other social channels
- Publishing thought leadership content on third-party channels, such as another advisor’s blog or the website of an esteemed financial news magazine
- Hosting virtual seminars or webinars that offer a deep dive into your chosen topic


Professional certifications, positive online reviews and[client testimonials](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-testimonials) can enhance your reputation as a thought leader. Certifications, such as a CFA designation, are evidence of your expertise in the topics you discuss, while reviews and testimonials act as a form of social proof in the trust your clients have in you.

## 3. Target AI Overviews and Local Search


Search engine optimization (SEO) refers to tactics that help a website rise in search rankings. The ultimate goal is to have your business rank at the top of results. AI overviews are changing the way SEO works for financial advisors and other businesses. Instead of simply focusing on[keywords](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-seo-keywords) and phrases that your ideal clients search for online, AI overviews look for content that is readable, answers searchers’ intent fully and is backed by expertise.


Targeting local clients, meanwhile, is another effective[digital marketing strategy](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/digital-marketing-strategies-for-financial-advisors) for financial advisors. Forty-six percent of all Google searches are conducted with local search intent, meaning the user is looking for a business or services in their geographic area.3 For example, if someone searches for ‘financial advisor near me’ or ‘wealth manager in \[your city\]’ and your business is near or at the top of the rankings, that dramatically increases the odds of the searcher reaching out to you.


Here are some common digital marketing strategies for improving your rankings in AI overviews and local search:


**Write for LLMs** Create content that directly answers search intent and is easy for AI tools to interpret, which may improve your chances of appearing in AI overviews.


**Claim and Verify Your Google Business Profile** Complete every profile field on your Google Business Profile, add photos and keep your information accurate to improve your visibility in local search.


**Ask for Reviews** Reviews can strengthen your Google Business Profile and support local visibility. Under the[SEC’s marketing rule](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/sec-marketing-rule-faqs) , advisors must avoid selectively soliciting or displaying favorable reviews.


**Optimize Your Site for Local Search** Use location-based keywords and, if you serve multiple areas, create dedicated landing pages for each market.


## 4. Leverage Short-Form Content


Video content allows financial advisors to connect with audiences in a more personal and engaging way. Short videos can help explain complex financial topics, share timely insights or answer common client questions in a format that feels approachable. According to HubSpot’s 2026 State of Marketing Report, short-form video, long-form video and live-streaming video are the top three ROI-driving content formats reported by marketers.4


Short-form may be particularly appealing if you have limited time to film, edit, and upload content. You can record a short 30-second to 1-minute video explaining a single concept or answering a question using your smartphone or basic video equipment.[TikTok finfluencers](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/personal-finance-influencers) like Humphrey Yang provided the blueprint for this type of content, but there are plenty of advisors finding success with[YouTube](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-youtube) Shorts. According to HubSpot, YouTube had the highest engagement rate for short-form video content in 2025, beating out TikTok and Facebook Reels.


You may focus on a single platform or all three; it ultimately depends on where your ideal clients spend their time online and what you have time for in your busy schedule. Batching multiple videos in a single session can help you keep your content calendar full, while marketing automation tools can assist with scheduling and posting videos to each platform you’re active on.


## 5. Build Community Compliantly Via Social Media


Social media offers an opportunity to build rapport with prospects and existing clients and have real conversations in an informal setting. According to HubSpot, 90% of marketers agree that building an active community on social media is crucial to a digital marketing strategy.


Community-building begins with creating content that’s interesting and engaging and reflects what your[ideal clients](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/ideal-client-profile-for-financial-advisors) care about most. Consistency is the second piece of the puzzle, as you need to show up for your followers regularly to gain their trust. Engagement is the third piece, as the goal is to talk *to* your followers, not just at them. You can encourage engagement by asking questions, inviting followers to share their opinions, hosting surveys or polls and replying to comments.


At each stage of the process, advisors must take care to leverage social media compliantly. For example, the SEC’s marketing rule prohibits advisors from sharing inaccurate or misleading information, or cherry-picking results when discussing investment performance. If you’re sharing testimonials on social media, those must be accompanied by the proper disclosures. And any marketing communications that take place on social media platforms must be properly archived.


Your[chief compliance officer](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/what-does-a-chief-compliance-officer-do) can help with developing a list of pre-approved topics and language for social media content. You may work together to create a process for ensuring compliance that involves submitting an initial draft or outline of content for approval, then resubmitting the final draft before publication to check for potential violations.


## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)


**Why Should Advisors Care About AI Search?**


More investors are relying on tools like ChatGPT and Gemini to conduct financial research and search for advisors online. Advisor website content that’s authoritative and designed to be read by large language models can boost that content’s visibility in AI search overviews. Greater visibility can translate to more website traffic and more prospects reaching out to schedule a[discovery call](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-discovery-meeting-agenda) .


**Is Traditional Financial Advisor Marketing Dead?**


Traditional marketing tactics are not dead but the most successful advisors understand the importance of a digital marketing plan. With more prospects using online searches to research and find advisors, a strong digital footprint is critical. Digital marketing strategies can enhance traditional marketing approaches like cold calling or[direct mail](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/direct-mail-marketing-for-financial-advisors) to help advisors reach a broader pool of potential clients.


**Should Advisors Hire a Digital Marketing Agency?**


Working with a[marketing agency](https://smartasset.com/advisor-resources/financial-advisor-marketing-agency) can take the pressure off your shoulders if you don’t have time to develop and implement a marketing plan. A reputable agency can analyze your business and ideal client base to create a plan that’s custom-built for you and help you put it into action. When comparing marketing agencies, consider the range of services offered, the level of support provided and the cost.


## **Bottom Line**


In the competitive field of financial advising, embracing digital marketing strategies can make a substantial difference in attracting and retaining clients. By incorporating a combination of these approaches into your digital marketing plan, financial advisors can establish a strong online presence, build credibility, and ultimately grow their client base in the digital age.
